_about: FIRST COMMAND, the first hour (the design director's ruling 129 and brief design-director/first-hour-brief.md; the words as cut by ruling 147; the door by ruling 141; the look by the art director's first-hour-look-brief.md). One list for both games, as the count of armies is (ruling 102): the lessons in order, their words, the deed line that earns each stamp, what each deed is called when an interface reports it ('does'), and when each comes due ('due', read by lessons.ts). Words in CAPITALS name controls; where a game calls a control something else, its own word stands in 'names' for that game and the design director is told. {place}, {province} and {city} are filled from the campaign in hand. Which lessons are done is kept with the player, not with the save, so a second campaign does not teach them again unless he asks.

door.label: First command
door.fresh: New here? Learn as you play.

setting: Staff notes for a new commander

groups.label: October 1939 · The city and the railway
December 1939 · Building, and the war is yours

lessons.head: The month
lessons.text: The war moves a month at a time. You give your orders, then END THE MONTH carries out everyone's at once. This card opens every month: read it first.

lessons.head: Pick up an army
lessons.text: Click the flag at {place} to pick the army up. Its card shows its corps. Lit ground is as far as it can march this month. Esc puts it down.

lessons.head: March
lessons.text: Right-click lit ground to send it there. Right-click friendly ground farther off and it keeps marching, month after month, until it arrives.

lessons.head: Attack
lessons.text: Right-click the enemy ground beside you. Before anything is spent, a card sets your army against theirs and gives the odds. Attack when its verdict favours you.

lessons.head: Next army, then end the month
lessons.text: NEXT ARMY (Tab) takes you to each army at the front with no orders. STAND THIS MONTH keeps one put. When it reads NEXT IN THE REAR, END THE MONTH.

lessons.head: Read the month card
lessons.text: Your fronts come first, then the world. Click a line to go to its place. A red band is a dated warning: never end a month without reading one.
lessons.deed: Click one line of the card.

lessons.head: A province falls with its city
lessons.text: {province} is not yours until {city} falls. Storm it now at the odds shown, or keep up the siege and let hunger, guns and bombers wear the garrison down.
lessons.deed: Storm it, or hold the siege a month.

lessons.head: By rail
lessons.text: The lit railway is where a train can take this army. Right-click a station dot to ride there: it takes the whole month. No train passes a red lamp.

lessons.head: A raid
lessons.text: Open STAFF and take the air war into your own hands. In the planner choose bombers, a raid and a target. The card sets BY DAY beside BY NIGHT: losses, damage and the guns that wait.

lessons.head: Build and rest
lessons.text: An army that stands a whole month rests and mends. Winter is for building: open the ARSENAL and place one order. Guns round a rail junction guard it against bombers.
lessons.deed: Place one order in the ARSENAL.
lessons.there: Order an artillery corps. Guns round a rail junction guard it against bombers. An army that stands a whole month rests and mends.

closing.head: The war is yours
closing.text: STAFF hands you each desk when you want it: research, building, envoys, agents, air, navy. GOALS shows what you are playing for. Every lesson is in the Guide.

tips.text: It will keep marching each month until it arrives. Any other order ends the march.
A red lamp: this line is cut. Send engineers to relay the track. Guns in this province would have stopped some of the bombers.

names._about: Each game's own word for a control, where it is not the list's. The browser game: END MONTH is its button; a railway journey is ordered on blue ground, not a station dot; a month card's line goes to its place by its pin; the arsenal is the BUILD page, which at Field command stands under STAFF (lesson 10's sentence is turned round to keep it to 30 words); the goals are on the REGION page; the Guide is the GUIDE on the top bar. The 3D game (the design director's ruling b425): the desks are YOUR STAFF and the raid is planned from the aircraft on the map; a month card's line goes to its place by its pin; the Guide is the GUIDE. (Its closing note says YOUR STAFF, which ruling b429 made room for by cutting both "the"s from the desks; NEXT IN THE REAR and STAND THIS MONTH read the same in both games.)
